change.title: fix(acp): parse native-binary npm shims so the Claude CLI probe launches
change.description: ## Summary Switching to the managed `claude-acp` agent on Windows failed with **\"Agent unavailable — Could not start \"node\". Check that the binary exists and is on your PATH.\"** even though Node.js was installed and on PATH. Two defects combined to produce that message: 1. **Windows shim parser gap.** Newer `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` npm packages install `claude.cmd` as a *native-binary* shim — a single quoted token invoking the bundled PE image: `"%dp0%\node_modules\@anthropic-ai\claude-code\bin\claude.exe" %*`. `parse_npm_cmd_shim` only understood the classic two-quoted `"" "

commits.message:
fix(acp): parse native-binary npm shims so the Claude CLI probe launches

Newer @<user>/claude-code packages install a claude.cmd that invokes
the bundled claude.exe directly — "<exe>" %* with a single quoted token —
instead of the classic "<node.exe>" "<script>" %* pair. parse_npm_cmd_shim
skipped that form, so the pre-spawn auth probe failed and the renderer
rewrote the resolver error against the managed agent's command, reporting
'Could not start "node"' although node itself resolved fine.

Extend the parser to accept a lone quoted executable tail and keep the
probe error verbatim when the file it names is not the spawned command.

Generated with [Devin](https://devin.ai)

files.patch:
@@ -30,6 +30,32 @@ describe('formatAcpSpawnError', () => {
       /"cursor-agent"/
     )
   })
+
+  it('keeps a resolver error that names a different binary verbatim', () => {
+    // Managed claude-acp spawns `node`, but a failed *pre-spawn* probe of the
+    // system claude.cmd names the shim — rewriting it against `node` would
+    // blame the wrong binary.
+    const raw =
+      'program not found or not executable: C:\\Users\\u\\AppData\\Roaming\\npm\\claude.cmd'
+    expect(formatAcpSpawnError(raw, { command: 'node' })).toBe(raw)
+    const result = classifySetupError(raw, { command: 'node' })
+    expect(result.category).toBe('spawn')
+    expect(result.detail).toBe(raw)
+
+    // The bare-name variant — e.g. the claude CLI probe failing to find
+    // `claude` on PATH — names a different program than the spawned `node`.
+    const bare = 'program not found on PATH: claude'
+    expect(formatAcpSpawnError(bare, { command: 'node' })).toBe(bare)
+  })
+
+  it('still rewrites a resolver failure that names the command itself', () => {
+    expect(formatAcpSpawnError('program not found on PATH: node', { command: 'node' })).toBe(
+      'Could not start "node". Check that the binary exists and is on your PATH.'
+    )
+    expect(formatAcpSpawnError('spawn C:\\tools\\node.exe ENOENT', { command: 'node' })).toBe(
+      'Could not start "node". Check that the binary exists and is on your PATH.'
+    )
+  })
 })
 
 describe('AmbiguousAuthError', () => {

@@ -21,6 +21,25 @@ export function formatAcpSpawnError(raw: unknown, config?: Pick<AgentConfig, 'co
   const message = definiteSpawnRejectionMessage(raw)
   if (!ENOENT_PATTERN.test(message)) return message
 
+  // Resolver-level failures already name the file they could not prepare
+  // after the last colon (e.g. `program not found or not executable:
+  // C:\…\npm\claude.cmd`). When that file is not the spawned command —
+  // managed `claude-acp` runs `node` while its *pre-spawn CLI probe* is the
+  // piece that failed — rewriting against `config.command` would blame the
+  // wrong binary, so the resolver's own wording stays.
+  const lastColon = message.lastIndexOf(': ')
+  if (lastColon >= 0) {
+    const namedPath = message
+      .slice(lastColon + 2)
+      .trim()
+      .replace(/^"|"$/g, '')
+    const namedBase = namedPath.split(/[\\/]/).filter(Boolean).pop()
+    const commandBase = config?.command?.split(/[\\/]/).pop()
+    if (namedBase && commandBase && namedBase.toLowerCase() !== commandBase.toLowerCase()) {
+      return message
+    }
+  }
+
   if (config?.command === 'npx') {
     return 'Could not run npx. Install Node.js and ensure npx is on your PATH, then try again.'
   }
